Assessment: Useful screening signal; weak basis for fine rankings
Evidence_or_reason: The report records anonymous department-level perceptions across nine relevant experience domains.
Practical_implication: Use it to generate questions and identify areas needing follow-up, rather than as a verified institutional finding.

Evidence_or_reason: Environment 15%, hands-on 15%; academics, faculty, senior-resident experience, work-life and mental health 12% each; stipend timeliness and safety 5% each.
Practical_implication: The stated formula is internally coherent. Weight choices reflect priorities, not demonstrated statistical validity.

Evidence_or_reason: All 1,710 complete rows agree within the +/-0.55-point bound from displayed rounding. Maximum observed absolute difference: 0.45 point. Thirty-eight rows have missing domain ratings.
Practical_implication: Preserve the published score. A rounded-domain recalculation is an audit, not a replacement. Missing-domain scores cannot be fully reproduced without the underlying data/rules.
Basis: Source pp 3-107; all-row coordinate and table checks

Evidence_or_reason: Score = 100 - 10 x weighted positive-experience rating. With 1-10 inputs, the attainable score is 0-90; 100 requires ratings of 0.
Practical_implication: The supplied report says ratings are out of 10, but does not establish whether 0 was selectable. Do not silently rescale the source scores.

Evidence_or_reason: The score includes hands-on training and academics alongside safety, environment and mental health.
Practical_implication: Weak academics can raise the index without proving bullying; poor training and mistreatment require different follow-up questions.
Basis: Analyst assessment of source p 2 domains

Assessment: A serious concern can be hidden
Evidence_or_reason: If every domain is 10 except safety at 1, the formula gives only 4.5 points and the report's Very healthy verdict.
Practical_implication: Inspect safety and mental-health ratings directly. Do not allow a favourable aggregate to cancel a serious concern. This example is hypothetical, not an allegation about a named department.

Assessment: No validation demonstrated in supplied PDF
Evidence_or_reason: Environment, senior experience, work-life and mental health may overlap; the PDF does not provide psychometric validation, reliability estimates or sensitivity analysis.
Practical_implication: The metrics have face validity as experience questions. Their weighting and interpretation need independent validation before calling the index a validated toxicity measure.

Evidence_or_reason: All 1,748 verdicts agree with the stated bands when read as <30, 30-<40, 40-<50, 50-<60, 60-<70 and >=70.
Practical_implication: No empirical evidence for these cut points is supplied. A 29.9 versus 30.0 distinction is not evidence of a meaningful clinical or educational difference.

Evidence_or_reason: The methodology says most departments have one or two responses, but no department-specific n is displayed.
Practical_implication: Every n is left blank in the workbook. Do not infer n from decimals or recommendation percentages, calculate confidence intervals, or rank close scores as precise differences.
Basis: Source p 2 and department table headers

Evidence_or_reason: Anonymous opt-in participation may select unusually positive or negative experiences. Current-resident status, cohort coverage and response rate are not documented in the supplied PDF.
Practical_implication: Anonymous reports may be truthful and valuable. Seek independent current and recently graduated residents across years; do not claim the survey represents every resident.

Assessment: A useful check with limited assurance
Evidence_or_reason: The revised methodology says near-identical repeat submissions within an hour count once.
Practical_implication: This does not by itself establish one verified person per response or prevent coordinated submissions. Ask how resident identity was checked without compromising anonymity.

Assessment: Revised table reconciles; cover retains old totals
Evidence_or_reason: Cover text contains older figures (2,758 residents, 1,018 colleges, 1,794 departments, 3 Oct) and revised figures (2,912 responses, 662 institutions, 1,748 departments, 6 Oct). Extraction matches revised 662/1,748/30 counts.
Practical_implication: Treat the supplied file as a mixed-version presentation. Use the reconciled revised counts, and keep 2,912 total responses separate from the stated 2,395 used for scores.

Evidence_or_reason: The cover says 2,912 responses and 2,395 used in department scores, a difference of 517. The supplied PDF does not reconcile this difference by exclusion reason.
Practical_implication: Request an anonymised inclusion/exclusion flow and per-department n. Do not assume all exclusions are duplicates or invalid responses.

Assessment: One-third of entries are not department reports
Evidence_or_reason: 577 of 1,748 rows (33.0%) carry an asterisk. The methodology says these use reports from the same institution or, failing that, the same specialty elsewhere.
Practical_implication: Duty_hours_estimated is a separate filter. These entries cannot substantiate that particular department's working hours. One additional row says Not reported.
Basis: Source p 2; independent count of source asterisks

Assessment: Too coarse for a workload comparison
Evidence_or_reason: Under 14 hours combines a very wide range; the PDF does not establish standard definitions for daily average, shift duration, on-call time or weekly hours.
Practical_implication: Ask for actual JR1 weekly rosters, 24/36-hour calls, post-call relief and days off. Do not convert bands into exact hours or infer they enter the score; they are not one of the nine weighted domains.

Evidence_or_reason: The revised note calls this the most common reported band. Twenty-five rows say Not reported. A band can conceal variation between years, deductions and delayed payment.
Practical_implication: Check the current official stipend order, bank-credit regularity and deductions. The PDF's stipend band is separate from its weighted stipend-on-time rating.

Evidence_or_reason: Nineteen rows have no percentage. A displayed 100% may be one respondent; 0% beside a low index is not necessarily an arithmetic error.
Practical_implication: Treat recommendation as a separate preference signal. It is not a probability of your satisfaction and its denominator need not equal the domain-score denominator.

Evidence_or_reason: Thirty-eight rows have at least one missing domain, 19 have missing recommendations, 25 lack stipend bands, and one lacks a duty-hours band.
Practical_implication: No zeros, replacement ratings or duty-hour estimates have been added. Ask how the original score handled missing values and per-domain denominators.

Evidence_or_reason: The report says name variants were merged. Three institution labels explicitly leave the campus unclear. A small number of rows combine program labels.
Practical_implication: Retain source names and MD/MS, DNB and Diploma labels. Confirm the exact department/campus before comparing with counselling data. These 662 entries are not all universities or all counselling-eligible colleges.

Evidence_or_reason: The revised source states data through 6 October 2026; it does not show response dates, PG year or faculty tenure beside each rating.
Practical_implication: Do not apply these scores as a measured 2025 baseline. Ask about current HOD, faculty, roster and recent changes before choosing a seat.

Assessment: No specific thread verified in this session
Evidence_or_reason: Reddit public search, JSON and RSS routes returned 403/network blocks. Search engines produced challenges or irrelevant results. No Reddit post/comment is being cited as read.
Practical_implication: The Reddit review sheet supplies clearly labelled search routes and an appraisal checklist. It does not establish that no relevant discussion exists, nor that the index is endorsed or rejected by Reddit.
